When I came out, I was ten. "I'm getting crushes on girls instead of guys," was what I told my mom. #NationalComingOutDay
But I always knew I was a lesbian. And until I was 25, it was something that I constantly fought to keep secret.
Others speaking out about their experiences, especially , allowed me to fully accept myself as I am. I'm gay, and I should be proud.
There are people that don't accept, of course. They don't understand. They don't care to. But my sexuality isn't about their discomfort.
I'm proud to be gay. I'm proud to be out. I'm proud to be another voice that can tell gay kids and adults alike, "Yes, it does get better."

"Gay" is a term for homosexuals, specifically men. "Queer" is an umbrella term for sexual and gender minorities who aren't heterosexual or cisgender. People who are cisgender are people who identify as the gender they're physically born as, like us.

I could be identified as "queer", for example, but I feel like "lesbian" is a better identifier for me. I have also seen some lesbians and other LGBTQ+ individuals identify as "gay" instead of saying "I'm a lesbian", "gay" is traditional for and about men loving men.

- Pick Up A New Hobby: I'm privy to writing myself, but there are a lot of hobbies people can do alone without much extra stuff. There are even tutorials on YouTube for most of these things. Wanted to stay something but didn't have the time? Now's your time.
